written.myAnswer: Each line represents one cyclist’s distance-time motion; its slope represents speed. The graph is not provided, so I cannot identify which cyclist travelled the most distance or had the greatest, lowest, or constant speed.

For constant speed, the area under the speed-time graph is a rectangle with area speed × time, which equals distance. For changing speed, divide the graph into small time intervals: each strip’s area (speed × time interval) gives the distance covered in that interval. Adding the strips gives the total distance, so the area under the graph equals the distance covered.
